item.title: Escaping WSL: Booting My Own Linux VM Through Hyper-V's HCS API
item.description: I’ve been building ephemerd, a daemon that runs self-hosted GitHub Actions runners with a fresh environment per job. On a Windows host, Windows jobs run in Hyper-V isolated containers, but Linux jobs still need a Linux kernel from somewhere. The obvious answer on Windows in 2026 is WSL2, and that’s what I used first. It worked great from my terminal and fell over the moment ephemerd became a real Windows service.
